findings.title: Public group members endpoint now truncates membership lists with no pagination UI
findings.body: The `members` action previously only paginated automatic groups (default limit 200) and returned the FULL member list for regular (non-automatic) groups. The new code unconditionally applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` / `offset` to every group, so any group (automatic or not) with more than 50 members will only return the first 50. However, the public-facing template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` and its route `group-members.js.es6` were not updated with any next/previous pagination controls (only the admin group page got pagination UI in group.hbs). Consequently, visitors to a public group's members page for any group with >50 members will silently see only the first 50 members with no way to view the rest — a visible functional regression.

findings.title: Breaking response shape change for GET /groups/:name/members.json
findings.body: The members endpoint previously returned a bare JSON array (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`). It now returns `{ members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. This is a backward-incompatible change to a public API endpoint; any external client, script, or integration that consumed the old array response will break. This change isn't mentioned/versioned in the PR description.

findings.title: Unbounded client-supplied limit on members endpoint
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` has no upper bound/clamp, and this unbounded limit is now applied to ALL groups (previously only automatic groups allowed an uncapped client-supplied limit, defaulting to 200). A client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g. `?limit=1000000`) forcing the server to query and serialize an unbounded number of rows, which is a resource-exhaustion/perf risk now exposed more broadly than before.

findings.title: Off-by-one bug in totalPages computation
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 users with limit 50), this yields totalPages = 2 instead of the correct 1 (should be `Math.ceil(user_count/limit)`). This causes `showingLast` (`currentPage === totalPages`) to be false on what is actually the last real page, so the 'next' arrow stays enabled, and clicking it loads a phantom empty page (offset clamped to user_count returns zero members) while the pager displays e.g. '2/2' with no content.

findings.title: No error handling for addMembers/removeMember AJAX failures
findings.body: `removeMember` and `addMembers` only chain a `.then` success callback that reloads the member list; there is no failure/catch handler. Unlike `save`/`destroy` (which show a `bootbox.alert` on failure), if the request fails (e.g., 422 for an automatic group, validation error, or network failure) the promise rejection is silently swallowed and the admin controller (admin-group.js.es6 `removeMember`/`addMembers` actions) also does not attach any failure handler. Users get no feedback when adding/removing a member fails.

findings.title: No tests added for GroupsController#members behavior/response-shape change
findings.body: The PR substantially changes `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members` (new paginated response shape `{members, meta}` applied to all groups instead of only automatic groups, plus a new default/unbounded `limit`). No spec file for `GroupsController` is included or updated in this PR to cover the new pagination defaults, the new JSON shape, or the regression for non-automatic groups with many members.

findings.title: Add-members input is not cleared after submission (acknowledged TODO)
findings.body: The `addMembers` action contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and indeed never resets `usernames` after a successful add. This leaves stale usernames in the input field after members are added, which is confusing UX and was merged as a known-incomplete feature.
